question: Which predeclared raw-byte support tier is the strictest one that yields at least two useful maintainable level-1 motifs in each immutable held-out UTF-8 file under the same four-quarter isolation used by the invalid maintenance R1?
hypothesis: At least one of five frozen descending-support tiers will provide >=2 eligible motifs in both held-out files while preserving positive calibration advantage over the baseline. The strictest feasible tier is selected mechanically as the lowest tier index meeting that cross-file cardinality rule.
authority: research-only schedule attribution; no model repair, deployment, external-model inference, scheduler, queue, or runtime authority

fixed_inputs.training_and_model: exact canonical WLM-LM-REAL-UTF8-BYTE-PILOT-R2 model construction and four training blobs
fixed_inputs.segmentation: same four contiguous raw-byte quarters per file as invalid maintenance R1; context resets at each quarter boundary
fixed_inputs.motif_universe: same fixed 256 selected canonical four-byte motifs

selection_rule: For each tier compute eligible motif count independently in each file. The strictest feasible tier is the lowest numeric tier index whose minimum eligible count across both files is >=2. If no tier is feasible, selected_tier_index=-1. No other tie break or post-result schedule choice is permitted.
validity_criteria: Exact parent, North Star, prior invalid-attempt identity, corpus blob identities, canonical learner, and four-quarter split match.
No model degradation, repair, candidate intervention, or outcome interpretation is performed.
Eligibility uses only frozen raw support counts and canonical-vs-baseline calibration top-1 gain.
All five tiers and the strictest-feasible selection rule are fixed before output.
No evaluation bytes enter training or motif selection.
Full Go regression passes and normalized result carries exact experiment identity.

classification_rules.supported: Validity passes and a frozen tier 0..4 yields at least two eligible motifs in both files.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but no frozen tier yields at least two eligible motifs in both files.
classification_rules.incomplete: Corpus or compute interruption prevents complete attribution.
classification_rules.invalid: Identity, split, tier construction, deterministic selection, capacity, or qualification criteria fail.

no_post_result_tuning_rule: Do not alter the five tiers, four-quarter split, canonical learner, corpus, metric definitions, or strictest-feasible decision rule after observing output.
